clue.text: It's no good running

parts.note: read as a description: running a business or project in a way that is no good

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shrug that running is pointless; really 'running' means managing, and doing that badly is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor administration or control of an organisation is exactly a bad job of running it.

clue.text: Scotsman and nearly all his people making plot

parts.note: Mac, from the Scottish surname prefix, is a crossword name for a Scotsman

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A Scot and almost his whole clan scheming together.
explanation.definitionFit: A machination is a scheming plot or intrigue, usually crafty and underhand.

clue.text: Instrument Yes then played with, always eschewing echo?

indicators.note: letters played with are toyed with and rearranged
always eschewing means every instance of the letter is avoided, so both of them go

parts.note: Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E; 'always' takes away both Es in the fodder

explanation.surface: A musical question about the prog band Yes, who toyed with keyboards while avoiding echo effects.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of YES THEN, remove both Es ('always eschewing echo'), and rearrange the rest (Y, S, T, H, N).
explanation.definitionFit: A synth is a synthesizer, an electronic keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Romantically involved, ditching Tom as secondary?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed
ditching means these letters are thrown out of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone in a romance drops their partner Tom, who becomes a mere sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantically involved' looks like one phrase; it is the fodder plus an anagram signal. Remove T, O, M from ROMANTICALLY and rearrange R, A, N, I, C, A, L, L, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancillary means subsidiary or supporting, playing a subordinate role.

clue.text: Men with lowered energy in Eastern lands recall trouble

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Asia is the eastern continent

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowered means a letter moves further down, to the end of the word

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Men with sapped energy in the Orient struggle to remember things.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the E of MEN down gives MNE, which goes inside ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a difficulty with remembering.

clue.text: Brought to guillotine at last, head rolling in European city

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word
rolling over means the word turns round, read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A French Revolution execution scene: a head rolls after the blade drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head rolling' suggests a beheading; really NESS (a headland) reversed gives SSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in western Germany's Ruhr region.

clue.text: Tees consumes gin, served up at one: clues initially incomprehensible

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the result is read upwards, backwards
consumes means one piece swallows the other

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so refers to himself as me
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The setter knocks back a gin and finds his own clues baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: ME around GIN gives MGINE; reversed, that is ENIGM. Then AT, I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means mysterious and puzzling, hard to make sense of.

clue.text: Company in ancient wood?

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asks whether there might be companions in an old forest.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd', a pair counts as company.

clue.text: Religious portrait Tees does?

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself is I
to do someone is to swindle or con them

explanation.surface: Asks whether the setter paints holy pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a devotional painting of Christ or a saint, especially in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: John is seen with child stars

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
a minor is a child in law

explanation.surface: A man called John is spotted out with his child.
explanation.walkthrough: John here is the toilet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis Minor, the Little Dog, is a small constellation containing Procyon.

clue.text: Last tsar going commando might some say?

indicators.note: some say means some people pronounce it this way, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: going commando means wearing no underwear, so knickerless

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that Russia's final emperor wore no underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a loose, non-rhotic accent, knickerless sounds like the tsar's name, hence 'some say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas II was the final Russian tsar, deposed in 1917.

clue.text: Ring back in no more than 59 seconds?

indicators.note: back means read the other way, backwards

parts.note: 59 seconds at most is under a minute, sub-min

explanation.surface: Promises to return a phone call within a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a halo, the luminous circle round a saint's head.

clue.text: Resistance insufficiently worn down?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a secret resistance movement, as in wartime

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as under-ground, too little ground down.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground is a covert movement fighting an occupying regime; under-ground plays on grinding.

clue.text: Admirer, ardent indeed, rebuffed in North and South for nothing

parts.note: a fan is an admirer

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North
S is the compass abbreviation for South

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so read backwards

parts.note: mad about something means ardent for it
ay is an old word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A keen admirer gets turned down across the country, all for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD + AY reversed is YADAM, placed between N and S. Fanny Adams (sweet Fanny Adams) is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet Fanny Adams is a British idiom meaning nothing at all.

clue.text: New conductor's function almost a disaster

parts.note: an electrical conductor's job can be earthing, connecting a circuit to the ground

explanation.surface: A fresh orchestra conductor's performance nearly ends in calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: The conductor is electrical, not musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, something that very nearly went wrong.

clue.text: Drink for example supplied with good meal (substantial according to Eustice)

parts.note: Scotch is whisky, a drink

explanation.surface: A drink and a good meal, with a nod to a minister's ruling on pub food.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2020 UK minister George Eustice said a Scotch egg counted as a 'substantial meal' under Covid pub rules. A Scotch egg is a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a snack food that a British minister famously classed as a proper substantial meal.

clue.text: Surge? This does, regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Asks what surges, and answers that this thing does it at regular times.
explanation.walkthrough: Tides really do surge regularly, so the surface also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide is a rising and falling flow of the sea, a surge of water.

clue.text: Taking most of bed, the fat lady?

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A large woman hogs most of the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'it ain't over till the fat lady sings': the fat lady is an opera singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a leading female opera singer, the stereotypical 'fat lady' who sings at the end.

clue.text: Booking weak comedian

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, weak in nerve
a card is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: A feeble comic being booked to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: In football (soccer), a booking is a caution shown by the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee books a player by showing a yellow card as a caution.

clue.text: Seductive singer links Garland with traditional stories

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories and knowledge
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A siren singer is associated with Judy Garland and old folk tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Garland sounds like Judy Garland, the singer, but it is the flower garland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a Rhine siren of German legend who lured boatmen to their doom with song.

clue.text: One in duet — that's ridiculous!

indicators.note: an outcry that something is absurd signals the letters are in a ridiculous order

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a single person performing in a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being united means joined together as one, a single whole.

clue.text: 5 in song for 7, which is a cover

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the answer to 7 is two, and a duet is a song for two
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing riddle about a song, read as a cover version.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet is a quilted bed cover filled with down or fibre.

clue.text: Branch specialised in launching carpeting line

parts.note: carpeting someone is giving them a rocket, a severe telling-off
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: A department that launches floor coverings along a line.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, a carpeting and a rocket both mean a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and technology of rockets, the field of propelling craft skyward.

clue.text: Mistake from egghead over stopping children's education?

parts.note: read as egg's head, the first letter of egg

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so going inside

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are basic schooling
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A clever person finds a slip in the schooling of children.
explanation.walkthrough: Egghead splits as egg + head: the first letter of egg. O goes inside RRR after the second R.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a blunder or slip, something done wrongly.

clue.text: I love us roaming around rough Kentucky location

indicators.note: around means wrapping about the other piece
roaming means wandering, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: feeling rough means feeling ill

explanation.surface: Someone declares love while travelling through rough parts of Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: I LOVE US rearranged gives LOUISVE, which goes around ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisville is the largest city in Kentucky, home of the Kentucky Derby.

clue.text: Apply lubricant round willy regularly

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: regularly means the even-placed letters of the word

explanation.surface: A smutty instruction about lubrication.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil something is to grease it so moving parts run smoothly.

clue.text: Overwhelming defeat — challenger at last exposed

indicators.note: at last means the final letter

parts.note: out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: A challenger's crushing loss finally laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a decisive, crushing victory over an opponent who flees in disorder.

clue.text: Was Rachmaninoff so prone to kleptomania?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: having a light touch on the piano keys, as the virtuoso pianist did

explanation.walkthrough: Rachmaninoff was a great pianist, so his fingers were light in the literal sense; the idiom means thievish.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-fingered is an idiom for given to petty theft, and literally describes nimble hands on a keyboard.
